intended_object: An internal step in the library's Navier–Stokes construction. It combines two phase constructions `F 0`, `F 1` over the same index set `ι` into one `PhaseFamily` indexed by `Fin 2 × ι`. I inferred this from the body and the docstring ("bundling `epsilon`, `p`, `pz`, `x0` and the required compatibility proofs").
explanation: The definition copies each field (`epsilon`, `p`, `pz`, `x0`, `theta`, `F`, `G`) from the component selected by the first coordinate of the index. That makes the two phase families into a single family indexed by `Fin 2 × ι`, which is just a disjoint union of the two families. This is bookkeeping for the library's own convex-integration-style construction, using its own `PhaseFamily` and `PhaseConstruction` structures. It has no standard counterpart in the mathematical literature and no corresponding notion in Mathlib, so it cannot be compared with a textbook object.
